object_description: three offset elongated pavilion-like school volumes
design_condition: Three offset volumes are placed centrally and subtly raised above the terrain to mediate between the surrounding buildings and railway, while generating varied outdoor spaces around the tree population.

positive.statement: The differentiated volumetrics respond to the specific situation and compose a coherent urban whole.
The geometry creates varied opportunities to play and spend time in the outdoor spaces.
The basic levels are functionally well solved, with flexible spaces and useful cloakroom-playroom relationships.
The reserve multi-purpose room can be used for extracurricular district events and as a reserve classroom.
The project impresses with subtle urban development and good operational use of the school.

negative.statement: The relatively large footprint leaves only narrow peripheral areas for children playing outside.
The clearly separated basic levels make collaboration between classes on the same floor difficult.
The toilets in the eastern part of the building are too far from the basic level.
The facade is not sufficiently geared toward school use and the pavilion-like expression conflicts with the situation and use.
The extensive glazing requires glare protection that restricts the optimal use of daylight.
Integral elements in the interaction between architecture and technology are missing.
The project has poor economic efficiency because of its large outer surface and complex construction.
